text:
Lia: FYI customer on private VPC seeing intermittent TLS handshake failures during streaming. They report connection resets mid-generation.

Sam: Do we have their repro steps + tcpdump?

Lia: Customer pasted these steps and output:

```
curl -v https://api.redwood-inference.co/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <key>" \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-test","input":"very long prompt...","stream":true}'

* Connected to api.redwood-inference.co (54.12.34.56) port 443 (#0)
* TLS handshake completed
> POST /v1/generate HTTP/1.1
> ...
* READ: Connection reset by peer
```

Lia: They also attached tcpdump from their NAT instance with lots of repeated SYN / SYN-ACK then RST while tokens are streaming. Excerpt they sent:

```
10:12:11.123456 IP 10.0.0.5.51234 > 54.12.34.56.443: Flags [S], seq 0
10:12:11.123789 IP 54.12.34.56.443 > 10.0.0.5.51234: Flags [S.], seq 0, ack 1
10:12:11.124000 IP 10.0.0.5.51234 > 54.12.34.56.443: Flags [R], seq 1
```

Nish: That R coming from 10.0.0.5 tells me the return path (client side) is dropping or rejecting the packet. If they're using AWS NACLs and those are locked to only allow 443, that will break state for long lived streams — NACLs are stateless and must allow ephemeral ports for both directions.

Sam: Quick checklist to ask customer to run before we change infra:
- curl -v --no-buffer to confirm partial data is received
- sudo tcpdump -i <iface> host 54.12.34.56 and tcp -w capture.pcap
- traceroute --tcp -p 443 api.redwood-inference.co

Lia: Customer said their SG outbound is 0.0.0.0/0:443 but NACL outbound only allows 80/443; ephemeral range is blocked. They also have an on-prem security appliance doing strict egress filtering.

Sam: Actionable remediation (explain to customer):
- For AWS NACL on the private subnet/NAT, add TCP allow for ephemeral range (32768-60999) for BOTH egress and ingress. NACLs are stateless, so you need two rules.
- Ensure any on-prem DPI/proxy/appliance allows return traffic to client ephemeral ports for long-lived TLS.
- Security Groups are stateful; usually outbound 443 is enough, but if SG egress is restricted add appropriate rules.

Lia: Suggested AWS CLI examples to share (update IDs/rule numbers as needed):

```
# allow ephemeral range inbound to subnet (so replies back to ephemeral ports aren't dropped)
aws ec2 create-network-acl-entry --network-acl-id acl-0abc1234 --rule-number 110 --protocol tcp --rule-action allow --egress false --cidr-block 0.0.0.0/0 --port-range From=32768,To=60999

# allow ephemeral range outbound from subnet
aws ec2 create-network-acl-entry --network-acl-id acl-0abc1234 --rule-number 111 --protocol tcp --rule-action allow --egress true --cidr-block 0.0.0.0/0 --port-range From=32768,To=60999
```

Nish: Also note intermediate devices (NGFW, IPS) sometimes terminate or reset long-lived TLS if they enforce idle or byte thresholds. If they have TLS inspection, try a bypass for api.redwood-inference.co during the test.

Lia: Customer widened ephemeral policy on the on-prem appliance and added the two NACL entries. They retested streaming and micro-captures show no more RSTs. Customer: "streaming stable, no more resets". :white_check_mark:

Sam: Great. Follow-ups we should recommend in KB:
- Explain how NACL statelessness interacts with ephemeral ports and long-lived connections
- Example tcpdump signs (S, S., then R from client)
- Quick CLI snippets for AWS

ingress-monitor-bot: Incident monitor: no ongoing anomalies for this customer in last 60m.

Lia: I'll draft KB entry and link to this thread. Closing once KB is up. Thanks all.
